what: Where the value of every per-tick input field comes from. `ports_gate.py` reads this and refuses to run green while an in-scope field has no row.
scope: structs whose name ends in `Input` or `Measurements` under include/foc/core/**

kinds.contract: a declared contract names the channel (`hal/...` a hardware port, `core/...` an injected instrument)
kinds.host: a C entry in foc_api.h hands it in
kinds.derived: the library computes it from other fields; the producer names the header that does
kinds.constant: a number off a datasheet or a tuned scale, not a measurement; no producer
kinds.unfed: the application measures it and this project offers no channel -- a debt, printed every run

fields.note: The three-phase sum, read by whatever bench the integrator injects. The bench is a structural requirement of the board check, so this one had a channel before the gate existed.
Per-phase current-sense offset, from the bench's own zero-current capture.
Which way each phase responded to a known voltage: that is wiring, and only a physical bench knows it.
Measured current ripple at a known duty; the bench's scope or shunt.

The value the check compares the measurement against, computed by the caller from L, R and the switching period. A reference number, not a measurement -- if this came from the bench the comparison would be tautological.
Dead-time volt-seconds, measured from the phase-voltage distortion.

The commanded dead time scaled by V_bus and the PWM period: the caller knows its gate drive and the library cannot measure it. `foc_axis_deadtime_v` is the arithmetic, but the dead-time and switching numbers are the caller's.
Produced by the electrical alignment routine, then read back here to be compared against its limit.
`RsEstimator` produces it; the board check only adjudicates the number.
The datasheet value the estimate is held against.
`FluxEstimator` produces it.
The datasheet value the estimate is held against.
The observer's own angle error against the sensor, which is what the board check is auditing.
Mechanical angle, for indexing the table.
Mechanical speed, used to fade the table out at speed.
The d-axis current the table is not compensating for; needed to keep the sum honest.
The current controller's output, not a measurement.
The current ceiling the compensation is not allowed to push past; configuration.
Electrical speed, from the observer or the sensor; the feedforward does not care which.
Phase currents, rotated to d-q by the caller.
The speed command, through the C entry.
Gain scheduling scale, per tick; the caller owns the schedule.
Integrator-limit scale, same schedule.
The position command, through the C entry.
Profile limit, configuration.
Profile limit, configuration.
Gain scheduling scale, as for speed.
Phase currents; the magnitude is the caller's arithmetic on them.
The DC link, which has been a required contract from the start.

The field this gate exists for: until 2026-11-12 the HAL had no temperature at all and every integrator wrote the same divider inversion. The contract landed in 8785ea7. Known limit, stated where it can be read: the contract exists and nothing assembles it into this struct yet -- that is the drive supervisor's job, and a green row here does not claim otherwise.
Electrical speed, for the flux-weakening guard.
The observer's own confidence, so the protector can distrust a flux estimate that has drifted.
Same source: whether that estimate is worth acting on.
The outer loop's output.
For the back-emf and field-weakening terms.
For the voltage ceiling the reference must respect.
For the current-headroom terms.
The reference the modulator is asked to realise; computed upstream in the control frame.
The modulator needs it to turn a voltage into a duty.
Present for single-shunt reconstruction, where the currents decide whether the sample window is usable at all.
